brief.summary: Equity futures are lower, led by Nasdaq, while Treasury yields rose across the curve and long-end yields approached multi-decade highs. The move is global, with UK, German and Japanese yields also higher. Oil gained on renewed Iran/Hormuz tanker attacks, and credit spreads remain tight despite record supply. The Fed is described as hawkish after Jackson Hole, with markets pricing a possible September hike even as some guests expect a hold. The dominant narrative is a global bond selloff driven by deficits, issuance, energy and central-bank tightening, with AI capex increasingly rate-sensitive. Tone is risk-off but orderly, with strong earnings and buy-the-dip views limiting pessimism.
